title: feat(spec): ISecurityService gains the effective-object-permission reader
body:
Fixes #19578

Clause-②: yes (widening)

Executes the maintainer's ruling (decision batch 156, item 5, letter A, 2026-09-18): 「`ISecurityService` gains an effective-object-permission reader, threaded through the engine so `evaluateOptionVisibility` populates `EvalContext.permissions`; a census of every `current_user`-bound predicate evaluation site comes first」.

**This PR is the `packages/spec` half only** — the declaration. The engine-side threading, `evaluateOptionVisibility` and the `packages/objectql` / `plugin-security` wiring stay on the engine card (objectstack-ai/objectstack#18783), which is `pm:blocked` on this one, together with the census the ruling orders first.

## What lands

`ISecurityService.getEffectiveObjectPermissions?(context?)`, returning a promise of a **readonly Record keyed by object name whose values are `EffectiveObjectPermission`**, declared in `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts`, plus five contract pins in its test file. One optional member on a published interface; nothing renamed, narrowed or removed.

The return type is the **published** one, not a new parallel shape. `EffectiveObjectPermission` (`@objectstack/spec/security`) is the entry type of the `objects` map that `GetEffectivePermissionsResponseSchema` already serves, and `@objectstack/formula`'s `EvalPermissions` — the type of `EvalContext.permissions`, the slot the ruling names — is that same readonly Record, verbatim. So the engine half hands the reader's answer straight into that slot with no reshaping, which is the whole point of single-sourcing it.

## Why the shape is settled WITHOUT the census

The claim comment flagged that this card must return `needs_decision` if the reader's shape cannot be settled before the census. It can, and here is the measurement rather than the assertion — three shape questions, each closed by a published contract:

- **Return type** — fixed by `EvalPermissions` in `packages/formula/src/types.ts:40`, which is the declared type of the ruling's own target slot.
- **Whole map vs. a per-object reader** — fixed by the permission predicate's own documented semantics: "an object the effective map does not mention is an object with no grant, and answers `false`" (`packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts`). A narrowed map is therefore indistinguishable from a measured denial, and the objects a predicate names live in the predicate's source, not at the site assembling the context. The map cannot be narrowed by the caller, so the reader takes no object parameter.
- **Failure stance** — fixed by the same door's "**Absent is not empty**" rule (`packages/formula/src/types.ts`): with no map at all `can()` throws; an EMPTY map is a real answer evaluating to `false`. So the reader must throw rather than degrade to an empty map — degrading would publish "this subject holds nothing" as a measured fact — and an absent METHOD must leave the caller passing no permission data at all, never an empty map.

What the census decides is *which sites* get threaded and *what context each holds*. Neither moves any of the three above: the context parameter is already a Partial of `ExecutionContext`, and narrowing for cost is refused by the second bullet. ⛔ No census was run here.

## Why a reader on the service, not a merge in the engine

`resolvePermissionSetsForContext` deliberately leaves the merge to the caller, "because two consumers legitimately project different subsets of the same sets". This map is the projection two consumers need to be *identical* — `/auth/me/permissions` serves it, and the permission predicate reads it — and the second consumer cannot tell a wrong map from a right one. `toEvalPermissions` already names the hazard at its own door: a hand-built permission map "has no shape of its own to be wrong against: it parses, `can()` answers from it, and the answer is a confident silent denial". One producer removes the second copy before it is written.

The two constraints the card carried over hold as read: `ExecutionContext.permissions` carries permission-set NAMES, so this is a new reader and not a re-projection of something already threaded; and the hard serial pair in `rule-validator.ts` is not this diff's surface — this diff touches no file in `packages/objectql`.

## Verification

Commands, with each exit code captured before any pipe and the gate's own verdict line read rather than a bare status:

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` — exit 0 (`check-dts-emitted: 34/34 declared declaration file(s) present`).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` — exit 0 (`tsc --noEmit`, `check:scripts-typecheck`, `check:test-typecheck`). This test file carries no `test-typecheck-debt.json` entry, so its budget is zero: the file’s seven `@ts-expect-error` pins compile as errors-that-must-exist, and an unused one would red this. ⚠️ This diff adds **one** of those seven — six are pre-existing at the base. An earlier revision of this sentence said 「three」, which was wrong; the mechanism is unchanged, because a zero debt budget makes every pin in the file self-falsifying.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/contracts/security-service.test.ts` — exit 0, 19 passed (14 before this diff).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` — results in the report comment on the card.
- The gate families were derived from the diff by `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, ⛔ not from a hand-rolled list. Per-family verdicts, and everything that derivation itself marks NOT MEASURED, are in the report.

**Consumer sweep, narrowed and declared.** A new OPTIONAL member can break a downstream implementor in exactly one way: a pre-existing `getEffectiveObjectPermissions` carrying an incompatible signature. `git grep` for that identifier across this repo and the pinned `../objectui` checkout returns this declaration and its pins and nothing else, so there is no implementor to conflict with — which is why the downstream consumer closure was not rebuilt. The counts and the lit control are in the report.

## Acceptance notes

- `/auth/me/permissions` in `packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts` builds this exact map inline today (the most-permissive merge, `seedSuperUserRestrictedObjects`, `foldWildcardSuperUser`, `clampManagedObjectWrites`, `annotateEffectiveApiOperations`). Moving it behind this reader is the natural second consumer and would make the endpoint and the engine provably one answer — but it is runtime work in another package, outside this card and outside the engine card as split. Noted, not filed: no carrier is in flight for that file.
